vm Virtual Machine > Resource Limits and Exit Codes

Resource Limits and Exit Codes

This page quotes verbatim all default values from src/sandbox.zig and the exit-code mapping from src/plugin.zig, and lists the policy (sa.vm.policy/1) and environment-variable fallback order. After reading this section you will be able to accurately predict, without reading the source code, the exit code and stderr output of any sa vm ... invocation under boundary conditions.

Resource Limit Items and Defaults

The following fields are defined in src/sandbox.zig::Limits. Except for max_call_depth / stack_headroom_bytes, all field defaults are null or 0, i.e. “no limit” — on the dev path with no flags, vm is indistinguishable from unhardened mode.

FieldTypeDefaultCLI flagenv fallbackpolicy.limits section
fuel?u64null (no charging)--fuel=NSA_VM_FUEL=N"fuel": N
wall_clock_ms?u64null (no time limit)--deadline-ms=NSA_VM_DEADLINE_MS=N"wall_clock_ms": N
mem_cap_bytes?u64null (no memory limit)--mem-cap-bytes=NSA_VM_MEM_CAP_BYTES=N"mem_cap_bytes": N
max_call_depthu32100_000 (default_max_call_depth)--max-call-depth=N——
stack_headroom_bytesusize256 * 1024 (default_stack_headroom_bytes)———
Notemax_call_depth and stack_headroom_bytes have no CLI/env switch, but even without any cap set, runaway recursion will not hard-crash: vm will first hit the TEB stack guard page (Windows) or the host stack, triggering an E_STACK_OVERFLOW panic with exit 235, rather than a 0xC0000005 abort.

Fuel Charging Formula

Quoted verbatim from src/sandbox.zig::blockCost:

cost = body_words * 1 + slow_words * 15 + call_words * 31 + terminator(1)
fast-arm 固定 = 4
空块也至少 = 1（否则 while(true){} 是免费的）

The corresponding constants are:

ConstantValue
block_cost_base1
block_cost_slow_op15
block_cost_call31
block_cost_fast_arm4
clock_check_interval_blocks1024

Wall-clock checking is lazy: it samples once every 1024 charged blocks; FFI / pthread / builtin / broker call boundaries force a sample. A blocking system call (stuck inside native FFI) cannot be interrupted midway.

Priority and Fallback Order

src/plugin.zig::applySandboxEnvFallbacks and the subsequent if (sandbox_options.xxx) |v| limits.xxx = v; implement the following priority:

  1. An explicit CLI flag always wins (and no conflict is reported; the effective value is echoed in the start event).
  2. env fallback: SA_VM_FUEL / SA_VM_DEADLINE_MS / SA_VM_MEM_CAP_BYTES / SA_VM_POLICY (note that SA_VM_POLICY is a fallback for --policy, not a fallback for a cap).
  3. The limits section of the policy file: after parsing, the three non-null fields fuel / wall_clock_ms / mem_cap_bytes are filled into Limits.
  4. Otherwise disabled.

The corresponding source skeleton:

if (parsed_policy) |*policy| {
    if (policy.limits.fuel != null)         limits.fuel          = policy.limits.fuel;
    if (policy.limits.wall_clock_ms != null) limits.wall_clock_ms = policy.limits.wall_clock_ms;
    if (policy.limits.mem_cap_bytes orelse 0 != 0) limits.mem_cap_bytes = policy.limits.mem_cap_bytes;
}
if (sandbox_options.fuel)         |v| limits.fuel          = v;
if (sandbox_options.deadline_ms)  |v| limits.wall_clock_ms = v;
if (sandbox_options.mem_cap_bytes) |v| limits.mem_cap_bytes = if (v == 0) null else v;
if (sandbox_options.max_call_depth) |v| limits.max_call_depth = v;

Memory Quota (QuotaAllocator)

src/sandbox.zig::QuotaAllocator wraps std.heap.c_allocator and performs a live_bytes + additional <= cap check before alloc / resize / remap; exceeding the limit returns null / false, which vm translates into an E_MEM_QUOTA panic (the two catch points of the .alloc / stack_alloc instructions + frame allocation). Note: the parse arena does not go through quota; quota only covers the execution-time exec_allocator.

Tracked metrics (not directly exposed by --stats, but mem_peak_bytes in the violation event is one of them):

  • live_bytes: bytes currently in use.
  • peak_bytes: the maximum instantaneous value during this process’s VM lifetime.

Exit Code and Panic Code Mapping

The top of src/sandbox.zig defines all reserved codes (the code_* constants); src/plugin.zig always computes the process exit code as 128 + code (code & 0x7f is used for panic, but the reserved codes are all < 128, so “+” and “+&0x7f” are equivalent).

codeNameExit codeTrigger condition
100E_CAPABILITY_DENIED228Policy denial (any of fs / http / env / process / extern.allow / ffi / threads / net_raw)
101E_FUEL_EXHAUSTED229Accumulated block-cost exceeds --fuel (or policy.limits.fuel)
102E_TIMEOUT230Wall clock exceeds --deadline-ms (sampled every 1024 blocks + at FFI/builtin boundaries)
103E_MEM_QUOTA231The execution allocator QuotaAllocator rejects alloc / resize / remap
104E_VERIFY_FAILED232 (reserved)Currently not triggered, reserved slot
105E_POLICY_INVALID233The --policy JSON fails schema validation (including unknown keys, non-absolute-path fs patterns, etc., fail closed)
106E_SANDBOX_MISCONFIG234 (reserved)--sandboxed used together with --policy / --allow-ffi
107E_STACK_OVERFLOW235Guest recursion exceeds max_call_depth or host stack headroom is insufficient (256 KiB)

All code_* constant names can be turned into human-readable strings via sandbox_mod.nameForCode (E_FUEL_EXHAUSTED, E_TIMEOUT, etc.), for convenient writing into events.

Event Protocol: sa-vm-event

On every startup, as long as any cap or policy is configured, vm first writes a start event line:

sa-vm-event: {"v":1,"event":"start","fuel":N|null,"wall_clock_ms":N|null,"mem_cap_bytes":N|null,"max_call_depth":N,"stack_headroom_bytes":N}

Each cap violation writes a violation event line:

sa-vm-event: {"v":1,"event":"violation","code":N,"name":"E_...","detail":"...","fuel_used":N,"wall_ms":N,"mem_peak_bytes":N}

Events are single-line JSON terminated by \n, and can be captured with grep '^sa-vm-event:'. The schema version field "v":1 is for future extension compatibility.

Policy Schema: sa.vm.policy/1

A file passed to --policy=foo.json must start with "schema": "sa.vm.policy/1". The following fields are read; unknown keys make parsing fail (fail closed) to avoid misuse of an old policy:

KeySubkeyRole
schema—Must be "sa.vm.policy/1"
limitsfuel / wall_clock_ms / mem_cap_bytesResource caps, overridden by CLI flags
externallow (string[])Layer 1 symbol allowlist; default-deny
fsread (string[]), write (string[])Glob path patterns; on Windows, matched after realpath normalization
httpallow (object[])Each object: host / methods / path / port
envstring[]List of environment variables that may be read / written
processspawn (bool) / exec (object[])spawn switch + exec path / argument allowlist
Warningfs patterns that are not absolute paths are directly rejected by policy.zig (fs_path_invalid). This includes .., junction / symlink escapes, 8.3 short-name bypasses, NTFS alternate data streams, and DOS device names such as CON / NUL / COM1... See the threat table in the header comment of src/policy.zig for details.

Typical Conflicts and Diagnosis Flow

Use one table for quick matching:

SymptomPossible exit codeWhere to look
An infinite-loop program runs foreverNone (--fuel not set) / 229Confirm whether fuel has reached 0; the fuel_used field of the violation event
A long task is interrupted midway230wall_ms close to wall_clock_ms
A large alloc is rejected231mem_peak_bytes close to mem_cap_bytes
Deep recursion crashes235Check whether it hit max_call_depth or the TEB guard page
call @fn is rejected at the parse stage228detail contains extern_not_allowed or a concrete DenyReason.label()
--policy=... did not take effect233Confirm the JSON schema header; there is no violation, but stderr has an "Invalid VM run policy" line
--sandboxed + --allow-ffi given together234stderr contains E_SANDBOX_MISCONFIG
panic(11) / assertion failure139 (=128+11)stderr contains PANIC[11]: ... (no backtrace)
